DOMAIN AUDIT d06 — query patterns / JSONB / FTS / N+1 / indexes
guerrilla production scale at audit: documents table < ~1000 rows (task=784, paper=87, all other types=0)

CONCEPT                                          VERDICT                 BASIS
------------------------------------------------ ----------------------- ------------------------------------------
FTS tsvector <-> query config match              already-good            generated col + query both 'english' (+'simple' slug); GIN present
search_vector GIN index                          already-good            documents_search_vector_idx GIN(search_vector), final def 20260614220000
title ILIKE '%v%' (typeahead) + similarity()     already-good            documents_title_trgm_idx GIN(title gin_trgm_ops) serves both
content @> X containment (sheet embeds)          already-good            documents_content_path_idx GIN(content jsonb_path_ops), 20260702130000
N+1 discipline (3 preload sites / 673 files)     already-good            genuine JSONB-doc economy; resolvers batched; no per-iteration Repo.get
pagination stability                             already-good            asc:d.id total-order tiebreaker on every LIMIT/OFFSET path
offset/limit DoS caps                            already-good            offset<=100_000, limit<=200/1000, ranking pool<=500
task_edges blocker-join coverage                 already-good            (from_id,kind)/(to_id,kind) btrees serve unmet_blocker_counts + blocks gate
scoped-list composite + null-partial index       already-good            (ws,proj,type,dataset_id) + partial (type,dataset) WHERE dataset_id IS NULL
lower(title)=lower(x) wikilink resolve           rejected-with-reason    no functional index; but recheck within 87-row paper partition, human-paced
content->'labels'/'tags'/'aliases' @> scalar     rejected-with-reason    bare-col GIN can't serve col->'k' @> form; recheck within type partition, human-paced
content->>'kind'/'lifecycle_status' task filters rejected-with-reason    un-indexed JSONB; recheck within 784-row task partition, sub-ms today
4 facet GROUP BY queries per search              rejected-with-reason    6 round-trips/search but on <100 rows, human-paced; GROUPING SETS = tidiness now
fetch_doc_with_draft = 2 point lookups           rejected-with-reason    2 indexed point reads; halving to 1 saves nothing material
ready_query content.dependencies gate            ADOPT (FILED)           regexp_replace wraps indexed doc_id -> seq scan; hottest path; scar-class growth

blocks.text: Finding 1 (ADOPT / FILED task-2c74954d53781113, priority 2, MEDIUM confidence)
ready_query dependency-gate seq-scans the task partition

content.value: ready_query/1 (api/lib/barkpark/tasks/queue.ex:82-109) backs every bp task ready / bp task next poll and the row-locked atomic claim. Its content.dependencies readiness gate is a correlated NOT-EXISTS whose inner documents t resolution matches deps with regexp_replace(t.doc_id,'^drafts\.','') = regexp_replace(dep.id,...). Wrapping the INDEXED doc_id column in regexp_replace makes documents_doc_id_type_dataset_id_index unusable, so the inner lookup narrows only via (type,dataset) to the task partition and then SEQ-SCANs it, recomputing the regexp per row. Run once per open/blocked candidate x once per dep, cost is ~O(candidates x deps x task_rows) on the most frequently polled query in the system. The task ledger grows monotonically (never deleted; 784 rows today, synced issue ids already ~2274), so it degrades super-linearly with project age.

Scar class: Same shape as the content-GIN fix (migration 20260702130000): an un-indexed JSONB/expression predicate on a high-FREQUENCY path over a growing table. Here it carries the exact frequency multiplier that fix cited (every agent polls ready) that the human-paced label/tag/alias containment filters do NOT — which is why those stay rejected-with-reason and this one is filed.

Contrast (why it is specifically axis-2): The twin-collapse axis (queue.ex:117-137) does the SAME drafts-strip but stays index-friendly: o.doc_id == regexp_replace(parent_as(:doc).doc_id, ...) puts the raw indexed column on the LEFT and the computed value on the RIGHT, so o's (doc_id,...) index serves it. Only the dependency-gate inner query wraps the indexed column on the left, defeating the index.

Proposed fix: Provably cheaper, no new migration: resolve deps through the raw doc_id unique index by matching BOTH spellings (the both-spellings trick already used in Content.Query.resolve_docs_by_ids/3): t.doc_id IN (dep.id, 'drafts.'||stripped, stripped) so t.doc_id stays bare and the btree serves the lookup; keep the lifecycle_status='done' recheck. Alternative: a functional index on regexp_replace(doc_id,'^drafts\.','').

Confidence: MEDIUM. Query shape confirmed by static read; wall-clock NOT measured — no local Postgres (local API boot broken: codelist OOM) and guerrilla exposes no EXPLAIN over HTTP. At 784 rows absolute latency is likely still small; the finding is the growth shape on the hottest path. The fix task carries the protective EXPLAIN/benchmark acceptance criteria (seq scan before -> index scan after, at N>=5000 seeded tasks).

FTS: the generated search_vector (title A / author B / category B / slug C 'simple' / body D, all 'english' except slug) matches the retriever's plainto_tsquery('english') and phraseto_tsquery('english'); documents_search_vector_idx GIN backs it. Title typeahead: search_documents_by_title's leading-wildcard ilike(title,'%v%') AND the retriever's similarity(title,term) are both served by documents_title_trgm_idx (GIN title gin_trgm_ops) — a leading wildcard that would otherwise force a seq scan is fully indexed. Containment: sheet_embed_targets' bare content @> embed is served by documents_content_path_idx (jsonb_path_ops), the migration that fixed the 2s-flush seq-scan. N+1: exactly 3 Repo.preload sites (codelist values->translations, studio_chat session->messages) — genuine normalized relations, not the JSONB doc body; wikilink/valueref/search-hit hydration is explicitly BATCHED (resolve_docs_by_titles_or_aliases, resolve_docs_by_ids, get_documents_by_ids) with 'N+1 is forbidden' comments; a Repo-inside-Enum.map sweep found only single-query aggregates, no per-row loops. Pagination: every LIMIT/OFFSET path appends asc:d.id for a total order so pages never skip/duplicate on ties. Blocker joins: task_edges (from_id,kind)/(to_id,kind) btrees serve both the ready blocks-gate and unmet_blocker_counts.

All rejected items reduce to ONE structural truth: un-indexed secondary predicates (lower(title), col->'key' @> scalar, content->>field equality) execute as RECHECKS within a type-partition that the (type,dataset) / (ws,proj,type,dataset_id) btree already narrows to — NOT whole-table seq scans. At guerrilla's real partitions (paper=87, task=784) each recheck is sub-millisecond, and every path is human-paced (render, typeahead, board view), lacking the loop-frequency multiplier that made the content-GIN case a scar. The team indexes reactively when a path actually hurts (the content GIN is the proof), and the Felix doctrine rejects speculative 'add an index' with no measured cost. These are logged so a FUTURE re-audit at a materially larger corpus can revisit — the trigger is partition growth, not code shape.

Primary tool was static analysis: extracted real WHERE/ORDER/JSONB-path shapes from Content.Query, Search.DocumentsRetriever, Tasks.Query, Tasks.Queue, then diffed against every documents/tasks/search index across the 131 migrations. Partition sizes came from the live guerrilla HTTP count API (?count=true). EXPLAIN was NOT run — no local Postgres (local API boot broken: codelist OOM) and guerrilla exposes no EXPLAIN surface — so every performance verdict that depends on plan choice is marked MEDIUM confidence and the one filed finding's acceptance criteria require the EXPLAIN/benchmark to be produced by the fix, not asserted here.

Proposed fix: Provably cheaper, no new migration: resolve deps through the raw doc_id unique index by matching BOTH spellings (the both-spellings trick already used in Content.Query.resolve_docs_by_ids/3): t.doc_id IN (dep.id, 'drafts.'||stripped, stripped) so t.doc_id stays bare and the btree serves the lookup; keep the lifecycle_status='done' recheck. Alternative: a functional index on regexp_replace(doc_id,'^drafts\.','').

Confidence: MEDIUM. Query shape confirmed by static read; wall-clock NOT measured — no local Postgres (local API boot broken: codelist OOM) and guerrilla exposes no EXPLAIN over HTTP. At 784 rows absolute latency is likely still small; the finding is the growth shape on the hottest path. The fix task carries the protective EXPLAIN/benchmark acceptance criteria (seq scan before -> index scan after, at N>=5000 seeded tasks).

Already-good (adopt-verified, no action)

FTS: the generated search_vector (title A / author B / category B / slug C 'simple' / body D, all 'english' except slug) matches the retriever's plainto_tsquery('english') and phraseto_tsquery('english'); documents_search_vector_idx GIN backs it. Title typeahead: search_documents_by_title's leading-wildcard ilike(title,'%v%') AND the retriever's similarity(title,term) are both served by documents_title_trgm_idx (GIN title gin_trgm_ops) — a leading wildcard that would otherwise force a seq scan is fully indexed. Containment: sheet_embed_targets' bare content @> embed is served by documents_content_path_idx (jsonb_path_ops), the migration that fixed the 2s-flush seq-scan. N+1: exactly 3 Repo.preload sites (codelist values->translations, studio_chat session->messages) — genuine normalized relations, not the JSONB doc body; wikilink/valueref/search-hit hydration is explicitly BATCHED (resolve_docs_by_titles_or_aliases, resolve_docs_by_ids, get_documents_by_ids) with 'N+1 is forbidden' comments; a Repo-inside-Enum.map sweep found only single-query aggregates, no per-row loops. Pagination: every LIMIT/OFFSET path appends asc:d.id for a total order so pages never skip/duplicate on ties. Blocker joins: task_edges (from_id,kind)/(to_id,kind) btrees serve both the ready blocks-gate and unmet_blocker_counts.

Rejected-with-reason (logged, not filed)

All rejected items reduce to ONE structural truth: un-indexed secondary predicates (lower(title), col->'key' @> scalar, content->>field equality) execute as RECHECKS within a type-partition that the (type,dataset) / (ws,proj,type,dataset_id) btree already narrows to — NOT whole-table seq scans. At guerrilla's real partitions (paper=87, task=784) each recheck is sub-millisecond, and every path is human-paced (render, typeahead, board view), lacking the loop-frequency multiplier that made the content-GIN case a scar. The team indexes reactively when a path actually hurts (the content GIN is the proof), and the Felix doctrine rejects speculative 'add an index' with no measured cost. These are logged so a FUTURE re-audit at a materially larger corpus can revisit — the trigger is partition growth, not code shape.

Method & honesty note

Primary tool was static analysis: extracted real WHERE/ORDER/JSONB-path shapes from Content.Query, Search.DocumentsRetriever, Tasks.Query, Tasks.Queue, then diffed against every documents/tasks/search index across the 131 migrations. Partition sizes came from the live guerrilla HTTP count API (?count=true). EXPLAIN was NOT run — no local Postgres (local API boot broken: codelist OOM) and guerrilla exposes no EXPLAIN surface — so every performance verdict that depends on plan choice is marked MEDIUM confidence and the one filed finding's acceptance criteria require the EXPLAIN/benchmark to be produced by the fix, not asserted here.
